Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a right apical cavitary lesion containing a mobile intracavitary mass with an air crescent sign, which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma; this finding aligns with pulmonary complications that can occur in patients with underlying lung disease or structural abnormalities associated with Marfan syndrome.
